arxiv-2107-04102.title: Splitting ring extensions
arxiv-2107-04102.creator: Gabriel Picavet and Martine Picavet-L’Hermitte
arxiv-2107-04102.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Gabriel Picavet and Martine Picavet-L’Hermitte. The paper deals with ring extensions R ⊆ S R\subseteq S and their lattices [ R , S ] [R,S] of subextensions and is mainly devoted to FCP extensions (extensions whose lattices are Artinian and Noetherian). The object of the paper is the introduction and the study of elements of the lattices that split in some sense ring extensions. The reason why is that this splitting was used in earlier paper without their common nature being recognized.

arxiv-2201-01944.title: Time as change
arxiv-2201-01944.creator: Marcello Poletti
arxiv-2201-01944.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Marcello Poletti. According to Aristotle ”time is the number of change with respect to the before and after” B1 . That’s certainly a vague concept, but at the same time it’s both simple and satisfying from a philosophical point of view: things do not change along time, but they do change and the measurement of such changes is what we call time.

arxiv-2306-01780.title: Simulation of a first prototypical 3D solution for Indoor Localization based on Directed and Reflected Signals
arxiv-2306-01780.creator: Sneha Mohanty, Milan Müller, Christian Schindelhauer
arxiv-2306-01780.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Sneha Mohanty, Milan Müller, Christian Schindelhauer. We introduce a solution for a specific case of Indoor Localization which involves a directed signal, a reflected signal from the wall and the time difference between them. This solution includes robust localization with a given wall, finding the right wall from a group of walls, obtaining the reflecting wall from measurements, using averaging techniques for improving measurements with errors and successfully grouping measurements regarding reflecting walls.

arxiv-2404-19472.title: Multi-label Classification under Uncertainty: A Tree-based Conformal Prediction Approach
arxiv-2404-19472.creator: Wenge Guo
arxiv-2404-19472.description: Abstract Multi-label classification is a common challenge in various machine learning applications, where a single data instance can be associated with multiple classes simultaneously. The current paper proposes a novel tree-based method for multi-label classification using conformal prediction and multiple hypothesis testing.

arxiv-2412-18373.title: Lu/Se Substitution Effect on Magnetic Properties of Yb-Based Zigzag Chain Semiconductor YbCuS 2
arxiv-2412-18373.creator: Fumiya Hori 1, Hiroyasu Matsudaira 1, Shunsaku Kitagawa 1, Kenji Ishida 1, Souichiro Mizutani 2, Hirotaka Shirai 2, Takahiro Onimaru 2
arxiv-2412-18373.description: Abstract Abstract We have investigated the changes in the magnetic properties on YbCuS 2 by Lu or Se substitutions from a microscopic perspective. In general, it is expected that nonmagnetic Lu substitution dilutes the magnetic Yb 3+ concentration, and that Se substitution induces the negative pressure in YbCuS 2 .

arxiv-2507-23354.title: Consistent N eff N_{\rm eff} fitting in big bang nucleosynthesis analysis
arxiv-2507-23354.creator: Sougata Ganguly, Tae Hyun Jung, Seokhoon Yun
arxiv-2507-23354.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Sougata Ganguly, Tae Hyun Jung, Seokhoon Yun. The effective number of neutrino species, N eff N_{\rm eff} , serves as a key fitting parameter extensively employed in cosmological studies. In this work, we point out a fundamental inconsistency in the conventional treatment of N eff N_{\rm eff} in big bang nucleosynthesis (BBN), particularly regarding its applicability to new physics scenarios where Δ ​ N eff \Delta N_{\rm eff} , the deviation of N eff N_{\rm eff} from the standard BBN prediction, is negative.

arxiv-2508-17310.title: Handling Students Dropouts in an LLM-driven Interactive Online Course Using Language Models
arxiv-2508-17310.creator: Yuanchun Wang, Yiyang Fu, Jifan Yu, Daniel Zhang-Li, Zheyuan Zhang, Joy Lim Jia Yin, Yucheng Wang, Peng Zhou, Jing Zhang, Huiqin Liu
arxiv-2508-17310.description: Abstract Interactive online learning environments, represented by Massive AI-empowered Courses (MAIC), leverage LLM-driven multi-agent systems to transform passive MOOCs into dynamic, text-based platforms, enhancing interactivity through LLMs. This paper conducts an empirical study on a specific MAIC course to explore three research questions about dropouts in these interactive online courses: (1) What factors might lead to dropouts?

arxiv-2509-15726.title: Training Variational Quantum Circuits Using Particle Swarm Optimization
arxiv-2509-15726.creator: Marco Mordacci and Michele Amoretti
arxiv-2509-15726.description: Abstract In this work, the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm has been used to train various Variational Quantum Circuits (VQCs). This approach is motivated by the fact that commonly used gradient-based optimization methods can suffer from the barren plateaus problem. PSO is a stochastic optimization technique inspired by the collective behavior of a swarm of birds.

plos-pone-0011304.description: PLOS ONE research article. The Pr55 gag (Gag) polyprotein of HIV serves as a scaffold for virion assembly and is thus essential for progeny virion budding and maturation. Gag localizes to the plasma membrane (PM) and membranes of late endosomes, allowing for release of infectious virus directly from the ce

pmc-10547447.title: Smoking, tooth loss and oral hygiene practices have significant and site-specific impacts on the microbiome of oral mucosal surfaces: a cross-sectional study
pmc-10547447.creator: Sheila Galvin, Sviatlana Anishchuk, Claire M Healy, Gary P Moran
pmc-10547447.description: We investigated bacterial colonisation patterns of healthy mucosa (buccal, tongue, palate and floor of mouth) in a cohort of adults in order to determine how smoking, tooth loss, plaque levels and oral hygiene practices impacted on mucosal colonisation. A total of 322 swabs were recovered from 256 participants, of whom 46% were current smokers.

pmc-11418243.title: Pharmacists’ prescribing of opioids in Nova Scotia under Health Canada’s Controlled Drugs and Substances Act temporary exemption during the COVID-19 pandemic
pmc-11418243.creator: Ronald Watema-Lord, Ingrid Sketris, Heather Neville, Mark Asbridge, Chiranjeev Sanyal
pmc-11418243.description: is was exacerbated in Canada, with apparent opioid-related deaths increasing by 127% (8444 vs 4724) from 2020 compared to 2019. 3 Pharmacists have addressed the opioid crisis through activities such as providing education, advancing harm reduction strategies and monitoring opioid use disorder (OUD).

pmc-12082162.title: Low-magnitude high-frequency vibration reduces prostate cancer growth and extravasation in vitro☆
pmc-12082162.creator: Amel Sassi, Kimberly Seaman, Xin Song, Chun-Yu Lin, Yu Sun, Lidan You
pmc-12082162.description: Prostate cancer (PCa) continues to rank among the most common malignancies in Europe and North America with significant mortality rates despite advancements in detection and treatment. Physical activity is often recommended to PCa patients due to its benefits in preventing disease recurrence and managing treatment-related side effects. However, physical activity may be challenging for elderly or bedridden patients.

pmc-12473254.title: Digital Push–Pull Driver Power Supply Topology for Nondestructive Testing
pmc-12473254.creator: Haohuai Xiong, Cheng Guo, Qing Zhao, Xiaoping Huang, Hossam A Gabbar
pmc-12473254.description: Push–pull switch-mode power supplies are widely employed due to their high efficiency and power density. However, traditional designs typically depend on multiple auxiliary circuits to achieve functions such as power-up control, voltage regulation, and system protection, resulting in structural complexity and difficulty in debugging.

pmc-12511389.title: Association of increased physical activity with greater fat mass loss following metabolic bariatric surgery: A longitudinal observational study
pmc-12511389.creator: Han Na Jang, Young Suk Park, Sung Hee Choi, Young Min Cho, Hak Chul Jang, Tae Jung Oh
pmc-12511389.description: Metabolic bariatric surgery (MBS) is an effective treatment for weight loss, but a significant proportion of patients undergoing MBS experience weight regain or muscle loss. Exercise is recommended for patients undergoing MBS, but inconsistent outcomes have been reported on the effect of exercise on weight loss.

pmc-12664568.title: Pleiotropic regulatory mechanisms and targeted therapeutic prospects of Galectin-3 in aging-related diseases
pmc-12664568.creator: Jiayu Yuan, Xiaoyu Dong, Yan Gao, Jianfei Nao
pmc-12664568.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Aging is a major risk factor for numerous chronic diseases, including Alzheimer's disease (AD), Parkinson's disease (PD), atherosclerosis (AS), type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), osteoarthritis (OA) and age-related macular degeneration (AMD). Galectin-3 (Gal-3), a unique β-galactoside-binding lectin, has emerged as a critical mediator in the pathogenesis of AD and other age-related disorders by modulating key mechanisms such as inflammation, oxidative stress, and apoptosis.

pmc-12732520.title: Knowledge Translation Initiative to Improve Interdisciplinary Approaches to Psychosocial Oncology Among Community Stakeholders in Rural Regions of British Columbia
pmc-12732520.creator: Melba Sheila D’Souza, Louise Racine, Ruby Gidda, Prashant Kumar Pradhan, Arsh Sharma, Karma Lalli, Ashwin Nairy, Alice Sheethal Rasquinha, Marta Tremolada
pmc-12732520.description: Background: This study reports on a community engagement knowledge-translation world café hosted in British Columbia, built on the research project “Enhancing cancer navigation for newly diagnosed, treated and post-treatment of people living with breast cancer in interior region”. The aim was to co-create a knowledge translation initiative with community stakeholders to enhance interdisciplinary approaches to psychosocial oncology.

pmc-13287009.title: Multifaceted regulation of thymic tolerance by pattern recognition cascades
pmc-13287009.creator: Soumyadeep Mukherjee, Paramita Paul, Arpita Kar, Subhasis Barik
pmc-13287009.description: During their development, progenitor T cells have to pass through a series of tolerogenic filters inside the thymus, which ensure the survival and developmental advancement of only those thymocytes which fruitfully recognize the host’s own MHCs conjugated with non-self antigenic peptides.

pmc-13385109.title: Association of non-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol to high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio (NHHR) with cardiovascular mortality in peritoneal dialysis patients: a prospective cohort study
pmc-13385109.creator: Yuening Zhang, Junjie Liang, Suchun Li, Kexin Ma, Dandan Zhang, Wei Chen, Qinghua Liu, Jing Yu
pmc-13385109.description: BackgroundThe association between non-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol to high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio (NHHR) and prognosis in patients with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) remains controversial. The aim of this study is to explore the association of NHHR with cardiovascular disease (CVD) mortality as well as all-cause mortality in peritoneal dialysis (PD) patients.

pmc-13585280.title: Functional organization and natural scene responses across mouse visual cortical areas revealed with encoding manifolds
pmc-13585280.creator: Luciano Dyballa, Greg D. Field, Michael P. Stryker, Steven W. Zucker
pmc-13585280.description: A challenge in sensory neuroscience is understanding how populations of neurons operate in concert to represent diverse stimuli. To meet this challenge, we have created “encoding manifolds” that reveal the overall responses of brain areas to diverse stimuli and organize individual neurons in stimulus-response coordinates according to their selectivity and response dynamics.

pmc-13625478.title: Retrospective case–control study of haematological indices and inflammatory ratios in the diagnosis of paediatric brucellosis
pmc-13625478.creator: Emine Hafize Erdeniz, Yeter Düzenli Kar
pmc-13625478.description: BackgroundBrucellosis is a common zoonotic infection in Turkey and other Mediterranean countries. In children, symptoms are usually non-specific, including fever, fatigue, arthralgia, and myalgia, which may complicate diagnosis. Haematological indices and inflammatory ratios have recently been studied as possible supportive markers in infectious diseases, but findings in brucellosis remain inconsistent.

pmc-13695477.title: Unique EEG signature of atypical absence seizures in SYNGAP1‐related developmental and epileptic encephalopathy
pmc-13695477.creator: Rainier Mark Loidor L Rapal, Joshua Chang, Douglas Nordli
pmc-13695477.description: wing and disorganization, with poor anterior–posterior gradient (Figure 1). There were frequent bursts of diffusely distributed and pleomorphic slow spike and wave interictal discharges. Ictal EEG during atypical absence seizures showed slow eyelid closure followed by occipitally predominant spike–wave discharges (Figure 2). This crescendoed into a generalized 2 Hz–2.5 Hz spike and polyspike and wave pattern, ending with diffuse slowing.

uslaw-usc-t18-s1657.description: United States Code, Title 18 (Crimes And Criminal Procedure); Part I (Crimes); Chapter 81 (Piracy And Privateering). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Whoever attempts to corrupt any commander, master, officer, or mariner to yield up or to run away with any vessel, or any goods, wares, or merchandise, or to turn pirate or to go over to or confederate with pirates, or.
